statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is at the top of the watch band and below the block threshold after an orderly, two-way US cash open.
recommendation: Elevated stress with tail below the block threshold. The narrow flagged window covers the remainder of the morning trend-decision period through the 15:30 UTC European cash close.
headline: Cash open produces a bought 95-point dip and a stalled NQ 40 points under the session high; Tail eases to 24 and the mapped state returns to WATCH
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 29,712.75 (+1.56%) inside a 29,247.75-29,753.25 session range, roughly 40 points below a high that was set before the 13:30 UTC cash open and has not been exceeded in the two hours since. The cash index is 29,415.15 (+1.62%) against a 28,945.06 prior close, having opened at 29,401.54, sold off to 29,305.90 and recovered to a marginal new session high of 29,421.38. That sequence matters for path risk: the opening auction produced a genuine 95-point retracement that was absorbed rather than a one-way extension, and futures have made a lower high during cash hours. The 13:28 UTC assessment placed Tail at 26 specifically on the risk of opening-auction continuation into an already aligned bullish regime; that checkpoint has now printed and resolved with two-way discovery, so Tail eases to 24 at the top of the watch band. Cross-assets remain aligned with the rebound but are no longer uniformly extending. VIX is 15.99 (-9.73%) against a 17.20 prior close, yet it has lifted off a 15.38 session low while the index holds near its high, a mild non-confirmation. The 10-year yield is 4.945% (-6.1bp) near its 4.941% session low, against 5.00% on the September 15 H.15 release, and the 2-year was 4.67% at that same observation. WTI is $100.34 (-2.04%) with a $99.15 session low as Saudi Arabia routes cargoes through ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, easing the supply premium created by the East-West pipeline strike. Semiconductors lead with SOXX +3.19% at $518.07, though also below its $520.42 high, and the S&P 500 at 7,630.92 (+1.05%) is likewise off its 7,646.60 high. The macro cluster at 12:30 UTC resolved without violent repricing: initial claims 196,000 against a 208,000 consensus, continuing claims 1,730,000, the Philadelphia Fed index 37.8 against 30.5 expected while cooling from 47.4, housing starts 1.275 million and building permits 1.394 million. The backdrop remains Wednesday's 25 basis point increase to a 3.75%-4.00% target range, the first hike since 2023, with projections pointing to the possibility of another move this year. That leaves a two-day relief rally inside a hawkish policy regime rather than fresh directional repricing. Stress eases to 55 in the elevated band on continued volatility decay, and Confidence is 87 on live cash, futures, volatility, rates, crude, breadth and verified macro evidence. Shared Finviz context was 126 minutes old with its futures section unavailable, so it was treated as stale and not used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the assessment spent most of its time in the low-to-watch Tail band, with one orange excursion to Tail 31 in the 19:00 UTC hour on Wednesday as the rate decision and the press conference drove a Nasdaq-100 sell-off. That move retraced into a flat close and Tail fell back to 16-20 overnight. Stress decayed steadily from 79 at the decision to 57 by early Thursday afternoon as volatility normalised, yields eased below 5% and crude fell on the Saudi rerouting workaround. The final ten hours carried a trend-up mode with Tail climbing from 18 to 26 as the European relief grind extended into the US cash open.
outlookSummary: The current 14:00 UTC hour holds Tail at the top of the watch band while the opening imbalance finishes clearing, then steps down through the US midday on the assumption that rotation replaces directional efficiency after the 15:30 UTC European cash close. A modest lift is carried into the 19:00 UTC power hour and the 20:00 UTC cash close because quarterly expiration positioning can compress late liquidity, which has not been observed. Overnight slots sit at 16-17 on the absence of scheduled catalysts rather than on observed structure. Conditional Tail then firms back through Friday's European expiration hedging window and into the US pre-open, where the 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release and the quarterly expiration open are the named checkpoints. Confidence declines with forecast distance because evidence quality degrades, not because the risk picture deteriorates.
